criteria.criterion: A full band whose last item is in-window is split and its own items are not stored.
criteria.plannedImplementation: SoldBackfillPlanner.Resolve: when the page is full (>=100 listings), the reported total is >100, and the last item's resolved sold date is still inside the window, and the band can still split (PriceBand.CanSplit), the planner returns a Split decision. MercariPriceBandCollector's backfill branch enqueues the band's children on Split and does not call MergeAndCountNew for that band's own page.
criteria.evidence: dotnet test tests/MarketMakerEtl.Tests.Unit --filter FullyQualifiedName~SoldBackfillPlannerTests|FullyQualifiedName~MercariPriceBandCollectorTests: both named tests pass (part of the 272/272 passing Unit run after the post-review fixes).

criteria.criterion: The cutoff search stores exactly the in-window items even with 2-3 out-of-order dates next to the boundary.
criteria.plannedImplementation: SoldBackfillPlanner.FindCutoff runs a binary search over the page (anchored on the already-known in-window first item and out-of-window last item), then ProbeMargin re-checks every position within +/-3 of the binary search's approximate boundary and takes one past the last in-window position seen in that probed range, so 2-3 local inversions at the boundary cannot cause an off-by-N truncation.
criteria.plannedVerification: SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_find_the_cutoff_tolerant_of_a_few_out_of_order_dates_near_the_boundary builds a page with 2 swapped dates straddling the true cutoff and asserts the stored count matches the true in-window count exactly; MercariPriceBandCollectorTests.Should_store_only_the_in_window_items_for_a_partial_band_even_with_local_order_inversions_near_the_boundary re-verifies the same scenario end to end through the collector.
criteria.evidence: Both named tests pass in the 272/272 Unit run. Manually traced the binary search + probe over offsets [1,5,3,7,9,11,17,19,21,23] days with a 15-day cutoff: true in-window set is indices 0-5 (6 items); the algorithm returns cut=6 despite the transposed 5/3 pair, matching the assertion.

criteria.criterion: Trading/no-date items are treated as in-window.
criteria.plannedImplementation: SoldBackfillPlanner.ResolveSoldDate: an item page with Status=='Sold' (covers Mercari's 'trading' and 'sold_out' states) but no parsable SoldDate resolves to the injected TimeProvider's current time (always inside a positive-day window; TimeProvider replaced a direct DateTime.UtcNow call in the post-review round so tests can pin 'now' with FakeTimeProvider). An item that is fully resolved (its detail page parsed) but has no usable date at all resolves to Resolved(null), and IsBeforeCutoff(null) is false, so it is always treated as in-window; an item whose fetch/parse genuinely could not be resolved after 3 retries is tagged Unresolved instead, which top-level Resolve() still treats as in-window for the newest/oldest checks (consistent with the same conservative rule) but which FindCutoff/ProbeMargin treat as unknown rather than in-window (see AC-5's post-review fix).
criteria.evidence: Both named tests pass in the 272/272 Unit run.

criteria.criterion: Scope item 4: count item-date lookups against the run's fetch budget and record them on the run.
criteria.plannedImplementation: SoldBackfillPlanner is constructed with a dedicated Scrape:MaxBackfillItemPageFetches budget (ScrapeOptions, default 400) as its item-page fetch cap -- no longer shared with DetailFetchOptions.MaxDetailFetchesPerRun, which serves the unrelated, later item-detail-fetch phase and defaulted far too low (50) for a real backfill (the 'ps5 controller' prototype needed 138 fetches). Each lookup retries up to 3 times (each attempt consuming budget) on a thrown exception or null parse result; once the budget is exhausted, ResolveDate returns Unresolved immediately rather than guessing 'in-window', and FindCutoff/ProbeMargin treat an Unresolved item as unknown (it can move the binary search's hi bound down but never lo, and is skipped rather than extending the in-window count), so an exhausted budget or a permanently-unresolvable item stops the planner from over-collecting instead of silently treating every unresolved date as in-window. SoldBackfillPlanner.BudgetExhausted surfaces this state; MercariPriceBandCollector threads it onto PriceBandCollectionSummary.BackfillBudgetExhausted, and SearchRunIssueFactory.AddBackfillBudgetExhaustedIssue records a 'SoldBackfillBudgetExhausted' run issue when it fires. ItemPageFetchesUsed threads through PriceBandCollectionSummary -> SearchCollectionResult.BackfillItemPageFetches -> ScrapeRunService's RunCompletionCounts -> a new ScrapeRunEntity.BackfillItemPageFetches column (migration) -> ScrapeRunView.
criteria.plannedVerification: SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_store_only_what_is_already_decided_when_the_item_page_fetch_budget_is_exhausted (budget exhaustion stops guessing), Should_resolve_the_date_after_the_item_page_fetch_fails_once_then_succeeds (retry), Should_not_let_an_unresolvable_midpoint_push_the_cutoff_later (tri-state cutoff math), MercariPriceBandCollectorTests.Should_flag_the_backfill_budget_as_exhausted_when_item_page_fetches_run_out (summary/issue wiring), CoreServicesDefaultsTests.Should_default_max_backfill_item_page_fetches_to_four_hundred, ScrapeLimitsConfigurationTests.Should_read_max_backfill_item_page_fetches_from_configuration, and ScrapeRunServiceTests.Should_record_backfill_item_page_fetches_on_the_completed_run.
